title: Astragaloside IV protects against high altitude hypoxia-induced cardiac injury through the CaSR-NF-kB and EGFR-PI3K-AKT-MDM2 pathways.
authors: Li, Xiaowen; Cao, Ruiqi; Zhang, Ling; Chen, Jie; Qin, Zhen; Huang, Danyi; Nie, Yazhen; Duan, Zheng; Pu, Lingling; Wang, Zirou; Li, Ran; Wang, Xinxing; Liu, Weili; Chen, Zhaoli
journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄芪甲苷对高原缺氧心脏损伤的保护机制，涉及蛋白-蛋白信号通路和分子对接，但无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Astragaloside IV (AS-IV), a bioactive compound renowned for its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-apoptotic properties, has not yet been investigated for its potential role in modulating cardiac function under high-altitude conditions. This study elucidates the cardioprotective effects of AS-IV against high-altitude-induced cardiac injury and explores the underlying molecular mechanisms. Under hypobaric hypoxia, we observed significant cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, as confirmed by comprehensive echocardiographic, histopathological, and molecular analyses. Remarkably, AS-IV administration effectively attenuated these pathological changes, restoring cardiac architecture and function while mitigating oxidative stress and apoptosis. Further in vivo and in vitro experiments revealed that AS-IV preserves mitochondrial integrity by enhancing membrane potential, ameliorating mitochondrial impairment, and modulating calcium homeostasis through the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR)-nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-kappaB) signaling axis. Network pharmacology-based screening identified key molecular targets, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K), protein kinase B (AKT), and mouse double minute 2 (MDM2), which were subsequently validated via molecular docking studies demonstrating strong binding affinities between AS-IV and these core proteins. Mechanistic investigations further revealed that siRNA-mediated EGFR knockdown or pharmacological activation of CaSR abolished AS-IV's cardioprotective effects, including its anti-apoptotic, antioxidant, and mitochondrial-stabilizing properties. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that AS-IV exerts its therapeutic effects through a dual-pathway mechanism involving (1) the EGFR-PI3K-AKT-MDM2 axis and (2) CaSR-NF-kappaB signaling. These insights position AS-IV as a promising candidate for the prevention and treatment of high-altitude-related cardiovascular diseases.
abstract_zh: 黄芪甲苷IV（AS-IV）是一种以其抗炎、抗氧化和抗凋亡特性著称的生物活性化合物，但其在高原条件下调节心脏功能的潜在作用尚未被研究。本研究阐明了AS-IV对高原诱导的心脏损伤的心脏保护作用，并探讨了其潜在的分子机制。在低压低氧条件下，我们观察到显著的心脏功能障碍、肥大和纤维化，这通过全面的超声心动图、组织病理学和分子分析得到证实。值得注意的是，AS-IV给药有效减轻了这些病理变化，恢复了心脏结构和功能，同时缓解了氧化应激和凋亡。进一步的体内和体外实验揭示，AS-IV通过增强膜电位、改善线粒体损伤以及通过钙敏感受体（CaSR）-核因子κB（NF-kappaB）信号轴调节钙稳态，来维持线粒体完整性。基于网络药理学筛选确定了关键分子靶点，包括表皮生长因子受体（EGFR）、磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶（PI3K）、蛋白激酶B（AKT）和小鼠双微体2（MDM2），随后通过分子对接研究验证了AS-IV与这些核心蛋白之间的强结合亲和力。机制研究进一步揭示，siRNA介导的EGFR敲低或CaSR的药理激活消除了AS-IV的心脏保护作用，包括其抗凋亡、抗氧化和线粒体稳定特性。综合来看，我们的研究结果表明，AS-IV通过涉及（1）EGFR-PI3K-AKT-MDM2轴和（2）CaSR-NF-kappaB信号的双通路机制发挥其治疗作用。这些见解将AS-IV定位为预防和治疗高原相关心血管疾病的有前景候选药物。
